title: PostgreSQL multiversion concurrency control (synthetic demo rubric, not validated)

criteria.description: Explains that an update writes a new row version instead of overwriting the old one, so readers and writers do not block each other.
Explains that each transaction reads a consistent snapshot decided by transaction visibility rules (for example xmin and xmax).
Discusses the costs of the design: dead row versions, table and index bloat, and the need for cleanup.
Connects VACUUM and autovacuum to reclaiming dead versions and to preventing transaction ID wraparound.
Notes isolation-level effects, such as read committed versus repeatable read, or that concurrent writes to one row still conflict.
Supports claims with a concrete mechanism or example rather than bare assertion.

references.title: PostgreSQL documentation: Concurrency Control
references.summary: PostgreSQL keeps multiple row versions; each statement or transaction sees a snapshot, so reads do not block writes and writes do not block reads.

references.title: PostgreSQL documentation: Routine Vacuuming
references.summary: VACUUM reclaims space held by dead row versions, updates visibility information and prevents transaction ID wraparound.
